opening.text: A carpenter does not wait for a big job to buy tools. He collects them one at a time. A hammer first. Then a saw. Then a level. Years later, when a hard job comes, his toolbox is ready.
Learning works the same way. Every skill and every truth is a tool. We gather them slowly, and one day we need them.

mainMessage.text: Learning is a gift and a responsibility. God wants us to grow in knowledge, the kind we get in school and the kind we get from Him. What we learn now blesses us and others for years.

blocks.text: **A gift with a purpose.** Tools are made for a job. God gave us the chance to learn, and He has work for each of us to do.
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
God gave you moral agency and the opportunity to learn while on earth, and He has a work for you to do.
Learning has a purpose.
**Your own toolbox.** No one else can fill your toolbox. Each of us has the responsibility to seek learning for ourselves.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
To accomplish this work, you have an individual responsibility to seek learning.
The toolbox is ours to fill.
**Not all tools are in the shop.** Some of the best tools are learned in life, in service and in prayer. Not every lesson comes in a classroom.
But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Some of your most important learning will be outside of the classroom.
Learning goes beyond the classroom.
**Fill the oil drop by drop.** Spiritual preparation is like oil in a lamp. It cannot be borrowed at the last minute. It must be gathered a little at a time.

They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Spiritual preparation must be acquired individually, drop by drop, and cannot be shared.
We gather it a drop at a time.
**Learning by faith.** A good tool is useful in the dark too. Learning by faith gives us confidence when things are uncertain. The Holy Ghost helps us know what is true.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Learning by faith will give you confidence and will help you navigate your way through times of uncertainty.
Faith lights the work.
**Pick up the tool and use it.** A tool in a box does no good. Learning has to turn into action and into who we become.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “To Learn, to Do, to Be” from the October 2008 general conference (Priesthood Session).
May we learn what we should learn, do what we should do, and be what we should be.
We learn, do and become.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when something they learned helped them later. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Daniel and His Friends Are Given Knowledge

blocks.text: Daniel and three friends were young men studying in a foreign land. They worked hard, and they stayed faithful to God.
As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Their study and their faith went together. God blessed both.

application.text: First, choose one thing you want to learn this month. It might be a skill, a language or a gospel topic.
Second, set aside twenty minutes, three days a week, to work on it.
Third, if you need help with school, work or finding direction, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God wants His children to learn. I know that He blesses those who study and seek Him. I have felt His help when I was trying to understand. I know that Jesus Christ is the source of all truth. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Old mapmakers drew maps one trip at a time. A traveler returned from a river, and the river went on the map. Another came back from a mountain, and the mountain went on. Slowly, the blank spaces filled in. Over many years, the map became useful.
Our minds are like that map. The more we explore, the more we know. And the more useful we become.

mainMessage.text: God wants us to keep exploring. He gave us minds, time and the desire to learn. Every truth we gain helps us serve Him and others better.

blocks.text: **The map has a purpose.** A map is made so someone can find a way. God gave us the chance to learn so we can do His work.
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
God gave you moral agency and the opportunity to learn while on earth, and He has a work for you to do.
The map is for the journey.
**Draw your own map.** Someone else’s map helps, but you have to explore for yourself. It is each person’s duty to seek learning.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
To accomplish this work, you have an individual responsibility to seek learning.
We explore it ourselves.
**Beyond the page.** Some of the most important places are not drawn in any book. We find them in the world, in people and in prayer.
But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Some of your most important learning will be outside of the classroom.
The best places are often beyond the page.
**One line at a time.** A mapmaker adds one line at a time. Spiritual preparation grows the same way, drop by drop. No one can do it for us.

They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Spiritual preparation must be acquired individually, drop by drop, and cannot be shared.
One line at a time.
**Exploring in fog.** Sometimes a traveler cannot see far ahead. Faith helps us keep exploring anyway. The Holy Ghost shows us what is true.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Learning by faith will give you confidence and will help you navigate your way through times of uncertainty.
Faith guides us in the fog.
**Walk the map.** A map is not worth much unless you travel it. What we learn becomes real when we act on it and grow into it.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “To Learn, to Do, to Be” from the October 2008 general conference (Priesthood Session).
May we learn what we should learn, do what we should do, and be what we should be.
We walk what we learn.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when learning something new opened a door. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Boy Jesus in the Temple

blocks.text: When Jesus was twelve, His parents found Him in the temple. He was sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.

And it came to pass, that after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
He listened and He asked. Good learning begins that way.

application.text: First, write down three questions you would like to understand better. Include at least one about the gospel.
Second, find one place to start looking for answers. It could be a book, a teacher or the scriptures.
Third, if you have questions that feel too big, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that learning draws us closer to God when we do it with faith. I know that He answers honest questions. I have found peace through study and prayer. I know that Jesus Christ is the Light of truth. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: On many farms, a barrel sits under the roof edge to catch rain. A single drop does not seem like much. But drop after drop, day after day, the barrel fills. In dry weather, that water is a gift.
Learning is a lot like that barrel. Each small lesson is a drop. Over time, they fill us up.

mainMessage.text: We do not need to learn everything at once. We learn a little each day, in school, in life and from God. Over time, those drops become a full supply.

blocks.text: **The rain is a gift.** Rain comes from above. The chance to learn comes from God, and He has work for us to do with it.
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
God gave you moral agency and the opportunity to learn while on earth, and He has a work for you to do.
The rain is a gift.
**Put out the barrel.** Rain does not fill a barrel that is left in the shed. We have to put ours out. Each of us has the responsibility to seek learning.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
To accomplish this work, you have an individual responsibility to seek learning.
We have to put the barrel out.
**Rain falls everywhere.** It falls on the field, the road and the roof. Learning happens in many places, too, not just in school. Some of the most important lessons come outside the classroom.
But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Some of your most important learning will be outside of the classroom.
Lessons fall everywhere.
**Drop by drop.** A barrel fills slowly. Spiritual preparation fills slowly, too. No one can pour theirs into ours.

They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Spiritual preparation must be acquired individually, drop by drop, and cannot be shared.
It fills one drop at a time.
**Water in the dry season.** When the dry season comes, the barrel is what you have. Learning by faith gives us confidence when times are uncertain.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Learning by faith will give you confidence and will help you navigate your way through times of uncertainty.
It carries us through dry times.
**Use the water.** Water in a barrel is no good unless someone uses it. Knowledge only helps when we act on it and become what we have learned.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “To Learn, to Do, to Be” from the October 2008 general conference (Priesthood Session).
May we learn what we should learn, do what we should do, and be what we should be.
We use what we have gathered.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a small, steady effort to learn paid off. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph Smith Reads James

blocks.text: Joseph Smith was a young man with a real question. He turned to the scriptures and found a promise that changed his life.

While I was laboring under the extreme difficulties caused by the contests of these parties of religionists, I was one day reading the Epistle of James, first chapter and fifth verse, which reads: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
He read, he asked and he acted. That is learning by faith.

application.text: First, pick a small daily habit, such as reading one page or one scripture verse.
Second, keep it up for one week, and notice what you learn.
Third, if you are struggling with a question about your faith, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that small, steady learning adds up. I know that God answers those who ask in faith. I have felt His help as I studied and prayed. I know that Jesus Christ is the source of wisdom. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Nobody builds muscle by watching others lift. You have to pick up the weight yourself. The first day is awkward. The second day is sore. But slowly, the weight gets lighter and you get stronger.
Learning is the same. It takes effort. Over time, the effort turns into strength.

mainMessage.text: Learning is work, and it is worth it. God gave us the chance to grow in knowledge and faith. When we put in the effort, He helps us become stronger than we were.

blocks.text: **A reason to train.** Athletes train for something. We learn for a reason too. God gave us the chance to learn, and He has work for us to do.
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
God gave you moral agency and the opportunity to learn while on earth, and He has a work for you to do.
We train for a purpose.
**Nobody can lift it for you.** A coach can guide you, but you do the lifting. Each of us has the responsibility to seek learning.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
To accomplish this work, you have an individual responsibility to seek learning.
We do the lifting.
**Train outside the gym.** Strength grows in daily life too: carrying groceries, climbing stairs. Learning grows in daily life as well, not only in school.
But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Some of your most important learning will be outside of the classroom.
Strength grows in daily life.
**One rep at a time.** Strength is built one rep at a time. Spiritual strength is built drop by drop. It cannot be borrowed from someone else.

They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Spiritual preparation must be acquired individually, drop by drop, and cannot be shared.
Strength builds a little at a time.
**Strength for the hard day.** On race day, you use what you built. When times are uncertain, the learning we did by faith holds us up.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Learning by faith will give you confidence and will help you navigate your way through times of uncertainty.
The training holds on hard days.
**Use the strength.** Strength is meant to be used. Learning is meant to make us better people, who then do good.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “To Learn, to Do, to Be” from the October 2008 general conference (Priesthood Session).
May we learn what we should learn, do what we should do, and be what we should be.
We use what we build.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when hard effort in learning made them stronger. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Solomon Asks for an Understanding Heart

blocks.text: Solomon became king while still young. He did not ask for riches. He asked for the ability to judge well.
Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
He knew he needed wisdom more than anything else. That is a good place to begin.

application.text: First, choose one area where you want to grow stronger this month.
Second, set a small weekly goal, such as reading, practicing or studying for thirty minutes.
Third, if you feel stuck, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that effort in learning builds real strength. I know that God supports those who try. I have felt myself grow through study and prayer. I know that Jesus Christ makes us more than we can be alone. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Before winter, a wise family fills the pantry. They put up jars in summer and stock the shelves in fall. It is a lot of work when the sun is out and nobody is hungry. But when the snow comes, they are ready.
Learning is a bit like filling a pantry. We do it before we need it. And when the hard season comes, we are glad we did.

mainMessage.text: We learn now so we are ready later. God gave us the time and the ability. When we fill our minds and our hearts with good things, we are prepared for whatever comes.

blocks.text: **Stock the pantry with purpose.** We do not fill shelves for fun. We do it because there is work ahead. God has work for each of us, and learning prepares us for it.
Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
God gave you moral agency and the opportunity to learn while on earth, and He has a work for you to do.
The pantry has a purpose.
**Your own shelves.** No one can fill your shelves but you. Each of us must seek learning for ourselves.
And as all have not faith, seek ye diligently and teach one another words of wisdom; yea, seek ye out of the best books words of wisdom; seek learning, even by study and also by faith.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
To accomplish this work, you have an individual responsibility to seek learning.
The shelves are ours to fill.
**Stock more than one kind.** A good pantry has more than flour. A good life has more than school. Some of the most important lessons come outside the classroom.
But to be learned is good if they hearken unto the counsels of God.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Some of your most important learning will be outside of the classroom.
A good pantry holds many kinds.
**One jar at a time.** A pantry fills one jar at a time. Spiritual preparation is the same, drop by drop. It cannot be handed over at the last minute.

They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Spiritual preparation must be acquired individually, drop by drop, and cannot be shared.
One jar at a time.
**When the storm comes.** When the roads close, the pantry feeds the family. When life gets uncertain, learning by faith gives us confidence to keep going.
And by the power of the Holy Ghost ye may know the truth of all things.

Sister Mary N. Cook, First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency, said this in her talk “Seek Learning: You Have a Work to Do” from the April 2012 general conference (General Young Women Meeting).
Learning by faith will give you confidence and will help you navigate your way through times of uncertainty.
The pantry feeds us in the storm.
**Share the harvest.** A full pantry is meant to be shared. What we learn becomes part of who we are, and it blesses others.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “To Learn, to Do, to Be” from the October 2008 general conference (Priesthood Session).

What we learn, we share.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when time spent learning prepared them for something they did not expect. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Mary Sits at the Savior’s Feet

blocks.text: Mary of Bethany made time to sit and listen to Jesus. Her sister was busy with many things. The Savior said Mary had chosen well.
And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word. But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
What we learn from the Savior stays with us.

application.text: First, find fifteen minutes this week to sit quietly with the scriptures.
Second, write down one thing you learned.
Third, if you need help finding time, direction or a way to continue your education, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that what we learn from the Savior can never be taken from us. I know that God helps us prepare for what is coming. I have felt peace when I was ready. I know that Jesus Christ is the Teacher of every true thing. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
